summary: Following D-GT21-S01-1 = C, the authors' 2024 copy is the public Dropbox folder linked from the EPIC lab page. It holds all six missing participants (AB12, AB15, AB17, AB19, AB23, AB28) with the same layout as the local 16: one session folder, osimxml, four modes with 12 channel folders each (ik_offset included, counts equal to conditions), and static/ik, static/ik_offset, static/markers. Together the six are 10,189 files, 7,005,667,538 bytes and 846 recordings (conditions files). Several checks support that the local 16 came from this folder. The root folder has the local root's name. The local README and SubjectInfo.mat are byte-identical to the folder's copies. Local AB14 equals its folder listing by path and byte size (1,722 of 1,722). One plan-only guarded-launcher spec per participant passes validate_spec in-process and binds the hashes of the acquisition script and its imported listing helper. Both scripts are written and await review. Nothing was launched or downloaded beyond two small root files. No José decision is needed.
findings: AB17: the 2024 trial counts equal the version 1 restoration plan (133). Size comparison of the local version 1 ZIP central directory against the 2024 listing: 1,464 of 1,466 version 1 files have equal size. 0 are version 1 only and 136 are 2024 only (133 ik_offset plus 3 static). 2 ramp/id files differ in size (ramp_1_r_01_01, ramp_6_r_01_04).

Listing modification times: in all seven listed participants the 2024-04-08 files are exactly ik_offset plus static. Every ramp/id file was rewritten on 2021-09-23/24, between version 1 and version 2. So version 1 checksums cannot vouch for ramp/id, and probably explain the 2 AB17 size differences. Dropbox times are metadata, not proof.
AB28 holds an extra osimxml/opensim.log dated 2026-10-11. The folder is a live working copy, so each acquisition must re-list and refuse on any change.

Download channel: the participant folder link with dl=1 returns a ZIP generated on request. A HEAD for AB12 gave Content-Length 1,165,363,841 against 1,165,001,799 listed bytes. There are no publisher checksums, so LocoHub's identity is the bound listing plus per-member SHA-256 recorded at download.

AB14 version 1 equivalence plan: superseded and not launched. The AB17 version 1 archive is already local, and the 2024 AB17 download answers the same question at CRC level without the extra 0.96 GB download. The AB14 plan is kept as a fallback only.

Six specs: guarded_launcher.validate_spec passed in-process. Each spec sets a 3,600 s timeout, 256 MiB address space, PM-01 memory reserves and a disk floor of 15 GiB plus twice the listing size on /mnt/s/locomotion_data (free now about 154 GiB). The output root is /mnt/s/locomotion_data/gt21_author_mirror_2024/<subject>, separate from the active source root and the version 1 folder, with receipts outside it.

Synthetic tests (tests/test_acquire_gt21_author_mirror.py, 19 cases; synthetic participant AB99; no network). They cover: a fake listing plus a fake ZIP, with and without the participant prefix, checking SHA-256, CRC32 and sizes against independently computed values; a member size mismatch and an unlisted member; a changed listing (extra opensim.log, changed time) refused before any download; a short disk refused before the output root is created; a pre-existing output root left untouched; a pre-existing receipt directory; receipts inside the output root; layouts missing ik_offset or static; a Content-Length outside its bounds; a wrong attachment name; a corrupted stored byte failing CRC; an unsafe member name; a STOP guard; and CRC comparison classification (expected, unexpected, v1-only, no overwrite).
Plan mode (no --run, no network) on the six real expected listings: all pass the layout check, including AB28 with its opensim.log.
The six saved specs were re-validated with guarded_launcher.validate_spec in-process. Every binding hash equals the current file, and no output root exists. Nothing was launched.

round_2_coordinator_request.request: Write the acquisition script and the AB17 CRC comparison script, add synthetic tests, bind the script hashes into the six specs, and do not launch.
round_2_coordinator_request.summary: Done. contributor_tools/acquire_gt21_author_mirror_participant.py implements the audit requirements. In order, it: refuses an existing output root or receipt directory, or either one inside a protected source root; re-lists the folder and refuses on any path, size, time or link change; checks disk (15 GiB reserve plus archive) and Windows memory; creates the output root exclusively; streams the dl=1 ZIP with SHA-256, a byte ceiling and a 1 MiB/s rate; publishes it with a no-clobber link; checks central-directory paths and sizes against the listing plus the GT21 layout (four modes x 12 channels, ik_offset, static); then streams every member for bytes, CRC32 and SHA-256 without extracting. All receipts go to acquisition_receipts/<subject> with exclusive creation; the output root holds only <subject>.zip. contributor_tools/compare_gt21_v1_vs_author_mirror_crc.py compares the local version 1 central directory with the manifest CRC32 values offline and splits differences into expected (2024-only ik_offset/static; ramp/id) and unexpected. The six specs now bind both scripts' hashes (the acquisition script imports the listing helpers from the review script) and add --receipt-dir; expected_output_names is now only <subject>.zip. The six expected listings are byte-unchanged.
review_points: The ZIP member naming of Dropbox folder downloads is not observed (no real download). The script accepts either all members prefixed with '<subject>/' or none, and refuses a mix or any unsafe name.
The Content-Length allowance is the listed bytes plus 1 KiB per file plus 64 KiB. AB12's HEAD value lies inside it: 362,042 bytes over the listing against an allowance of 1,878,016.
The re-list takes about 8 minutes (about 95 requests) inside the 3,400 s script deadline and the launcher's 3,600 s timeout; the download is capped at 2,700 s at 1 MiB/s (AB19 needs about 1,203 s).
Changing the review script, for example after verifier edits, changes a bound hash; the specs must then be regenerated with the plan subcommand.

round_3_verifier_fixes.S-1: Every check now runs on <subject>.zip.partial: central directory, layout, per-member CRC32/SHA-256 and the post-download re-list. member_manifest.json is written and <subject>.zip is linked (no-clobber) only after all checks pass. On any failure after the download, the bytes are kept as <subject>.zip.rejected (falling back to .partial) and the path is recorded as rejected_path; a rejected archive never carries the final name. Tests: the size-mismatch and CRC-corruption cases now assert the output root holds only <subject>.zip.rejected and no manifest.
round_3_verifier_fixes.S-2: After the download and member hashing, the folder is re-listed and compared with the bound listing (paths, bytes, modification times, folder link). Any difference, including a same-size edit (changed time), is refused, recorded as listing_differences_after_download and not published. The deadline is re-checked after this listing. Tests: a lister whose second call changes one file's time is refused with .rejected and no manifest; a clean run calls the lister exactly twice.
round_3_verifier_fixes.optional_taken: Symlink members (external_attr) are refused now; test added.
round_3_verifier_fixes.audit_wording: acquisition_script_requirements now states the actual Content-Length rule: listed bytes up to listed bytes + 1 KiB per listed file + 64 KiB, with no HEAD request by the script. The survey HEAD receipt is labelled as a survey-only request. The requirements also list the check-before-publish order and the post-download re-list.
round_3_verifier_fixes.not_taken: Dropbox revision_id comparison: the bound expected listings keep path, bytes and ts only, and adding revision_id would change the reviewed listings. The ts check already catches a same-size edit.
round_3_verifier_fixes.timing: The two re-lists take about 8 minutes each (about 95 requests at about 5 s per request, measured on 2026-10-31). With a download of about 1,003-1,203 s at 1 MiB/s and 1-2 min of hashing, AB19 needs about 38 min, under the 3,400 s script deadline and the 3,600 s launcher timeout.
